questions.question: Where is `plan-json report REQ-NNN` registered, and which handler receives it?
Trace the handler to the Planner module. Is report already implemented or only advertised?
Find an existing test for report output or its CLI integration; explain the exact behavior it asserts.

title: UI ownership and similarly named reports

questions.question: Which page and function render the plan before approval? Trace its caller.
Does that approval panel currently include the structured Planner report? Cite the actual render path.
The application also has a Review tab and REPORT.md. Are these the same report or a different lifecycle stage?
Find the reusable report producer and its presentation-independent shape. Identify the adapter boundary a future UI would use, without implementing it.

title: History projection and misleading nearby telemetry

questions.question: Trace `plan-json history --kind ...` from argument validation to its result producer. When is REQ-NNN rejected?
What exact context dimensions and task kinds are accepted? What happens to unknown fields or invalid values?
Find the returned quality, duration, retry and consumption measurements. Are any of them currently observed numbers?
Why does existing per-route M2 quality or attempt telemetry not automatically populate these Planner measurements?
Locate tests that demonstrate unknown output and prevent leaking route identities. State what these tests do not establish about live performance.

title: Whole DAG recommendation versus READY reservation

questions.question: Trace Scheduler start into whole-plan route mapping. Does it include blocked/dependent tasks or only READY tasks?
Find the concrete bridge to M2 and the bounded joint allocation. Is it one decision per task or one batch operation for the map?
Where are planned routes/unavailable reasons persisted, and what prevents repeating the map on restart?
Does whole-plan mapping reserve executor capacity or launch work? Locate the component that really reserves.
Trace READY assignment after account quota changes. Is the old planned model/profile blindly reused?
Where are quota refresh failures converted into unknown/unavailable facts, and how is the request timestamp tied to fresh observations?
Find an existing integration/regression test for plan-time routes versus execution-time revalidation or nonreservation. Explain its actual scenario.

title: Tier floors, comparable quality and effective account allocation

questions.question: Locate the real task-tier floor calculation. Explain the effects of high/extreme complexity, scope, coupling, duration and risk. Does medium risk alone force a higher tier?
Trace creation of candidate model/effort/profile/account identities. Is account identity simply a provider name?
Trace quota sampling preflight. How are aliases of one effective account grouped, is refresh always forced, and what bounds the work?
Locate hard eligibility filters for unsupported sources, auth/runtime and stale/unknown/exhausted quota. Can a good quality score bypass them?
When can quality rank routes? Trace minimum verified samples, uncertainty intervals and cross-route selected-level comparability.
Without comparable quality, what is the actual lexicographic order? How are missing or incomparable duration/cost facts handled?
Does the actual whole-plan adapter supply contextual quality assessments and API prices to that ranking? Separate policy capability from currently wired evidence.
Trace batch matching by effective account. Can two profile aliases manufacture capacity, and is a persisted batch a durable execution reservation?
Find tests that cover floor variation and account alias/capacity behavior. Identify any runtime facts about actual account quotas that this source snapshot cannot prove.

title: Extreme: crash, lost acknowledgement, stale events and independent verification

questions.question: Reconstruct the path from READY selection to a durable start order and M3 acceptance. Identify ownership and transaction boundaries, including when external calls happen.
Suppose M3 accepted a start but its acknowledgement was lost and M1 restarts. Trace how M1 decides whether to resend; identify the same-key protection in M3.
If the attempt lease expires and the executor query returns unknown, what happens to task, attempt, resource holds and retry eligibility? Cite the real branches.
Contrast query not_found for a pending unsent start versus not_found after delivery. Which branch allows safe redelivery and which records loss?
Trace an execution_finished event all the way to task completion. Is clean process exit or claimed success sufficient, and who may accept the work?
During VERIFYING, a later executor query says unknown or failed. Does reconciliation override the verifier? Locate the exception for operator action.
Trace duplicate event IDs, wrong plan/revision, old attempt IDs and wrong fencing tokens. Explain the incident-event exception rather than applying one blanket rule.
What happens if cancellation arrives before pending start delivery versus while work may already be running? Are holds immediately discarded in both cases?
Locate M3 restart recovery for PREPARING/RUNNING/SETTLING. What persisted process/shim/result facts are checked, and what remains uncertain instead of launching a duplicate?
Trace how an opaque M2 reference is bound back to the approved plan/task and account before M3 launch. Can a stale or mismatched reference silently fall back?
Find executable tests covering lost-ack restart, unknown-hold retention and stale/duplicate/verifier handling. Give distinct examples and explain their assertions; do not run them.
State the limit of the end-to-end guarantee. Does this source prove exactly-once effects at an arbitrary external provider, automatic quality acceptance, or live-account availability?
